newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta index down as big caps undergo correction.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta index down as big caps undergo correction.

text.p: Jakarta stocks fell further during the midsession on Friday as big-capitalised stocks, led by Telkom, continued to be corrected, brokers said.

At the lunchbreak, the Jakarta Composite Index was down 4.50 points, or 0.62 percent, to 724.66 points. Losers led gainers by 54 to 34, with 60 counters unchanged. Total volume was about 358 billion rupiah.
Telecommunications firm Telkom, which has the heaviest weighting on the index, fell 125 rupiah to 3,975 rupiah on a volume of 581,500 shares in what brokers said was profit-taking.
Blue chips Sampoerna and its competitor Gudang Garam as well as Astra International, Bank Negara Indonesia and Bank International Indonesia were the targets of profit-takers.
"I guess some foreign fund managers have started squaring their portfolios ahead of the summer holiday. This a cyclical trend every year," the research head a large local brokerage said.
He added the market would be return to normal sometime in August or early September.
Some investors, particularly local buyers, were actively snapping up medium and small-sized stocks which were considered cheap and which had been recently neglected, brokers said.
Smaller firm Suparma, retail firm Multipolar, Panin Life, and Panin Insurance were among the target of local buyers, brokers said.
Meanwhile, sustained buying interest was seen in blue chip Indocement. It rose 225 rupiah to 4,350 rupiah on a volume of 3.2 million shares on what brokers said was speculative interest.
"There is a rumour in the market saying Indocement is going to take some corporate action but it is unclear what kind of action," a broker with a foreign firm said.
Indocement's investor relations officer said the firm had no plans which were not known by public. He declined to give any further comment.
Brokers said the index's downward trend was likely to continue in the afternoon session with continued profit-taking in blue chip stocks expected.
